main_text.p: ut primùm pōtificem videt, detecto capite illum, genu terram tangens, veneratur: & iterum, quùm appropinquat ad gradus sedis, genu flectit; demum ad pontificis pedes pervenit, illos in reverentiam servatoris devotè osculatur. pontifex hilari vultu cæsarem aspiciens, ad osculum manus & oris recipit. tum cæsar iterum genu flectens auri massam ad pedes pontificis offert, habetque verba ad pontificem, gratias agens pro honore suscepto, pro ut ei videbatur. pontifex benignè ei respondens eum sublevat, & summa charitatis declaratione amplectitur. & stante ibi ad dextram pontificis cæsare, pontifex recipit imperatorem ad osculum pedis, & manus: regem verò, si quis adesset, ad osculum pedis, manus, & oris: alios autem prælatos, proceres, & nobiles cæsaris ad osculum pedis tantùm, Hæc Mar-cellus istè. En verò inauditam & intolerabilem Romanensium superbiam. His adde Alexandri III. papæ facinus, quod refert Jacobus Philippus Bergomensis monachus in supplemento chronicorum p.299. Inito fœdere inter imperatorem Fridericum & pontificem, Alexander summus pontifex confestim ad januas templi divi Marci euangelistæ accessit, & ibidem universo adstante populo, imperatori iussit, ut se humi pro-sterneret,

page.notes: Right page: cut off by the scan edge and set in very small, dense type; only the first few letters of each line can be read, and those readings are doubtful. Left page: the right-hand "Hæc Mar-cellus istè" is italic. Possible reference mark at the left margin beside "in supplemento" was not clearly legible and is not transcribed. Long s in the original is printed as s and rendered here as s. The ct ligature in "amplectitur" is rendered as ct.
